message.content:
Yes—you can file a noise complaint with the City of Atlanta’s local authorities.  
In Atlanta, noise‑related violations are handled by the **City of Atlanta Police Department** (and, in some cases, the **Department of Public Safety** or the **Code Enforcement Office**). Here’s how you can do it:

| Step | What to Do | Where to Go / Who to Call |
|------|------------|---------------------------|
| 1 | **Gather details** – Note the time, location, type of noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs), and any relevant evidence (photos, videos, or recordings). | — |
| 2 | **File a complaint online** – Use the City of Atlanta’s official portal: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> (or the “311” app). Search for “Noise Complaint” or “Public Safety.” | City of Atlanta 311 website/app |
| 3 | **Call 311** – If you prefer speaking to someone, dial **311** from any phone in Atlanta. The dispatcher will route your call to the appropriate department. | 311 (within Atlanta) |
| 4 | **Contact the Police Department** – For urgent or ongoing disturbances, you can call the Atlanta Police Department’s non‑emergency line: **(404) 656‑2000**. | Atlanta Police Department |
| 5 | **Check the Noise Ordinance** – The city’s noise ordinance (found in the Atlanta Municipal Code, Title 10, Chapter 10) specifies permissible decibel levels and quiet hours. Knowing the exact rule can help you describe the violation accurately. | Atlanta Municipal Code (online) |
| 6 | **Follow up** – After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. Keep it handy if you need to check the status or provide additional information. | — |

### Quick Reference

- **Atlanta 311**: 311 (within Atlanta) or <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311>
- **Atlanta Police Non‑Emergency**: (404) 656‑2000
- **Noise Ordinance**: Atlanta Municipal Code, Title 10, Chapter 10 (available online)

### Tips

- **Be specific**: Mention the exact address or intersection, the type of noise, and the duration.
- **Provide evidence**: If you have a recording or photos, attach them when you file online.
- **Check quiet hours**: Atlanta’s quiet hours are typically 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. on weekdays and 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. on weekends. Violations during these times are easier to prove.

If you’re unsure whether a particular noise is a violation, you can also call 311 for guidance before filing a formal complaint.
